display_name: Insurance Act 2015 (UK) under one top-level goal — application, fair presentation and the Schedule 1 remedies, warranties (s 10), terms (s 11) and fraudulent claims (s 12), and the amount payable on a claim — and those three goals

others: a fair presentation was made in (ia-presentation.l4)
there is a qualifying breach in … given … and (ia-presentation.l4)
the remedy for the presentation in … given … and (ia-presentation.l4)
the breach of warranty … suspends liability for a loss on (ia-terms-and-fraud.l4)
the insurer may rely on the non-compliance in (ia-terms-and-fraud.l4)
fraud excludes liability under … for an event on (ia-terms-and-fraud.l4)

scope: Goal-focused, at the user's direction: ss 1, 2(1), 3, 8, 10, 11, 12, 22 and Schedule 1 Part 1 of the revised text as at 4 May 2017. Inputs: knowledge under ss 4-6, materiality, what the insurer would have done, premiums and claim amounts, dates of breach, remedy, loss and fraud. Left out on purpose: variations, basis clauses (s 9), group insurance, late payment (s 13A), good faith and contracting out, Part 6.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-18 (tests-independent.l4, 109 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read); one failed (para 5 'if the insurer so requires') and the encoding was corrected; its remarks also led to Parts 3-4 applying to consumer contracts and a REFUSE before 12 August 2016. The pipeline has not been run.

forks.F1: Lost Schedule paragraph numbers and para 6 formula: printed order; X = premium charged ÷ higher premium × 100.
forks.F2: Relevant period: 18 months beginning 12 Feb 2015 end 11 Aug 2016.
forks.F3: A higher premium is a different term.
forks.F4: Para 5 applies only when the different terms lower the claim.
forks.F5: s 10(2): loss strictly after the breach day and before the remedy day.
forks.F6: s 11: reliance taken as excluding liability for the loss.
forks.F7: s 12(2)(a): events strictly after the day of the fraudulent act.
forks.F8: Consumer contracts: Part 2 not applied; Parts 3-4 apply.
forks.F10: Remedy is the most the insurer may do.
